blocks.content: Ladakh's tourism circuit draws directly on the geography (Chapters 1-2) and monastic heritage (Chapter 10) already covered — this chapter consolidates the key destinations by name, a straightforward but high-value table-based memorisation area.

cells: UT's main hub; Leh Palace (Chapter 3), old town bazaar, gateway to most onward destinations
Sand dunes (unusual at this altitude), double-humped Bactrian camel rides, Diskit and Hunder monasteries
Colour-changing high-altitude lake extending across the LAC; major tourism draw, especially following its feature in popular Indian cinema
Quieter, less-visited high-altitude lake; Ramsar wetland and key wildlife habitat (Chapter 11)
Remote, rugged valley; base for the famous winter 'Chadar Trek' (walking on the frozen Zanskar River) and white-water rafting in summer
A well-known optical-illusion site where vehicles appear to roll uphill; a popular roadside tourist stop
Commemorates the 1999 Kargil War (detailed in the companion J&K GS volume, Chapter 11); a major heritage/military-tourism site
Distinctive eroded badlands landscape surrounding Lamayuru Monastery (Chapter 10)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The 'Chadar Trek' (walking on the frozen surface of the Zanskar River in deep winter) is a globally noted, extreme-adventure-tourism activity unique to Ladakh's Zanskar Valley — a frequently tested distinctive-tourism fact.

items: High-altitude trekking (including routes through Markha Valley, Nubra, and Zanskar) is a major draw for both domestic and international trekkers, given Ladakh's combination of dramatic scenery and relatively well-developed trekking infrastructure compared to some other high-Himalayan regions.
River rafting on the Zanskar and Indus rivers (particularly around the Nimmu 'Sangam' confluence, Chapter 2) is a popular summer adventure activity.

Motorcycling/road-tripping the Srinagar-Leh and Manali-Leh highways has become a globally recognised adventure-tourism circuit, particularly popular among domestic Indian tourists, contributing significantly to the region's peak-season tourism economy.
Leh Palace, Nubra Valley (Khardung La), Pangong Tso (Chang La), Tso Moriri, and Zanskar Valley are the flagship destinations.
Chadar Trek = winter trek walking on the frozen Zanskar River, a globally distinctive Ladakh-specific adventure-tourism activity.
Kargil War Memorial, Dras, commemorates the 1999 Kargil War.
Magnetic Hill = well-known optical-illusion roadside attraction near Leh.
